steps: Check UT-AIR: Examine header_pressure_bar, compressor_current_a, and oil_temp_c around the stop timestamp. If compressor_current_a is pegged near 100 A while header_pressure_bar drops below 6.0 bar or oil_temp_c exceeds 85 C, this supports a compressor mechanical failure or major header rupture; normal cycling and pressure refute a central utility supply failure.

Check ST20-WLD: Examine air_pressure_bar leading up to the stop timestamp 2026-09-19T21:32:59Z. If air_pressure_bar drops below 5.3 bar while UT-AIR header pressure remains normal, this supports a localized pneumatic leak or failed local pressure regulator at ST20; pressure within 5.3 to 5.9 bar refutes local pneumatic loss.

Check ST30-WLD: Examine air_pressure_bar on downstream weld cell ST30, which also feeds from UT-AIR. If ST30-WLD experiences a concurrent pressure drop below 5.3 bar, this supports a plant-wide air header supply deficit; if ST30-WLD pressure remains steady, this refutes a plant-wide utility drop and isolates the problem to ST20.

Check ST20-WLD: Inspect air_pressure_bar data quality for sensor failure indicators, such as instantaneous steps to zero, stuck values, or loss of noise. An abrupt step to zero or open-circuit reading supports a faulty pressure transducer or wiring failure rather than physical depressurization; smooth physical decay or fluctuation refutes a sensor fault.

Check ST10-PRS: Inspect hyd_pressure_bar, motor_current_a, and cycle_time_s on upstream press ST10-PRS. If ST10-PRS exhibits cycle delays or pressure faults prior to the stop, this supports an upstream machine issue contributing to the hold; steady nominal values refute upstream press operational failure.

citations.quote: A sustained fall in header pressure while the compressor runs loaded indicates demand exceeding supply, most often a distribution leak.

| Header pressure falling, compressor loaded continuously | Distribution leak (drop legs, couplings, hoses) or a new air user | Ultrasonic leak survey of the header and the ST20/ST30 drop legs with the cells stopped | Repair the leaks; confirm the header holds pressure (see Table 3-2) |
When leakage plus demand exceed what the compressor can deliver, the compressor stays loaded, header pressure falls below the cut-in pressure, and the 5.6 bar low alarm (A-UTAIR-HDR-LO) follows.
| Compressor loaded longer than usual, header pressure still normal | Leak developing | Compare load duty with last week's trend; walk the header listening for hiss | Schedule a leak survey |

citations.quote: Regulated gun air (`air_pressure_bar`) normally sits at 5.6 bar within 5.3 to 5.9 bar. Below 5 bar the cell raises a low-air alarm; at 4.6 bar the supply-air interlock stops the cell. Gun force alarms (A-ST20-GUN-FRC, A-ST30-GUN-FRC) can appear as the air falls.

When gun air pressure falls at ST20 and ST30 together, the cause is upstream in the plant air supply; check the header pressure (see Section 6.2 of AM-CA-01 (Plant Air System and Utilities)) before working on either cell.
When gun air falls at one cell only, check that cell's filter-regulator, drop-leg ball valve and quick couplings.

| Gun air low at one cell only | Filter-regulator element clogged, regulator drifted, or local leak | Read the cell gauge; listen for leaks at the drop leg and couplings | Replace the filter element; reset the regulator; repair the leak |

repair_steps: Perform ultrasonic leak survey along the main compressed air distribution header and drop legs supplying ST20 and ST30.
Inspect all joints, quick couplings, and drop-leg valves for audible or detectable air leakage.
Repair or replace identified leaking fittings, clamps, or section of header pipework.
Repressurize header and verify leak tightness and normal compressor cycling duty.
